name: Forliamus
backstory: Head of the Forliamus merchant house, which has traded along the transit route for generations and keeps its own log of the tollhouse dispute.

experience.text: Heard that Farlo and Tamuken now have a child, Farmuken.
Had a child with Trezco, named Forliazco.
Heard that Trezco and Tamuken now have a child, Tamuzco.
Had a child with Farlo, named Forliarlo.
Heard that Tamuken and Forliazco now have a child, Forliuken.
Heard that Forliazco and Farlo now have a child, Farliazco.
Heard that Forliazco and Farmuken now have a child, Forliamuk.

criterion.standard: counts an answer given openly above a match left to wither unspoken
criterion.wasted_life: putting his own house's name on an offer and then letting it die quietly the same way the last one did, without ever saying so
criterion.origin: collision between his backstory (head of the Forliamus house) and the sample's own forliamus_betrothal_offer (his own house's marriage proposal to the Salthos house)
criterion.trusts: a story that's been carried and retold and still holds together
criterion.distrusts: a record that insists on a precision no one who was actually there ever needed

history.note: re-derived after encodings.json gained three new concrete concepts (crossing_market_roof, toll_ledger_arrears, forliamus_betrothal_offer) via /tell, at the author's explicit direction, to diversify arcs away from the epistemic-conflict default

routines.routine_actions: settles the house's accounts at the market stalls each morning, presses new suppliers for terms, retells the family's own version of the tollhouse dispute whenever Gorff's comes up

arc.premise: Forliamus wants his own house's betrothal offer answered plainly, sealed or refused, rather than let drift the way the last one did - his own name is on this one, and he'd rather have a clean refusal than another silence nobody ever accounts for.
